title.zh: 卷465 列傳二百五十二 徐桐附：豫师 豫师子：承煜 刚毅 赵舒翘 启秀 英年 裕禄附：廷雍 毓贤附：李廷箫
title.en: Volume 465 Biographies 252: Xu Tong With: Yu Shi, Yu Shi Son: Cheng Yu, Gang Yi, Zhao Shuqiao, Qi Xiu, Ying Nian, Yu Lu With: Ting Yong, Yu Xian With: Li Tingxiao
title.raw: 卷465 列傳二百五十二 徐桐附：豫师 豫师子：承煜 刚毅 赵舒翘 启秀 英年 裕禄附：廷雍 毓贤附：李廷箫

sentences.zh: 列傳二百五十二

translations.literal: Biographies 252
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 252

sentences.zh: 徐桐剛毅趙舒翹啟秀英年裕祿毓賢

translations.literal: Xu Tong, Gang Yi, Zhao Shuqiao, Qi Xiu, Ying Nian, Yu Lu, Yu Xian
translations.idiomatic: Xu Tong; Gang Yi; Zhao Shuqiao; Qi Xiu; Ying Nian; Yu Lu; Yu Xian

sentences.zh: 時擅訂約，下群臣議，乃條摘其不可行者：曰、各城定界；

translations.literal: At that time Chonghou had arbitrarily concluded a treaty with Russia; when it was referred to the court for discussion among all officials, [Xu Tong] itemized what could not be accepted: namely, fixing boundaries for the cities of Ili and Tarbagatai;
translations.idiomatic: When Chonghou took it upon himself to negotiate the Russian treaty, the matter was laid before the full court. Xu Tong listed the terms that could not be accepted: delimiting the cities of Ili and Tarbagatai;

sentences.zh: 曰、通商；

translations.literal: namely, opening trade in Xinjiang and Mongolia;
translations.idiomatic: opening trade in Xinjiang and Mongolia;

sentences.zh: 曰運貨迳至漢口；

translations.literal: namely, transporting goods straight through to Hankou;
translations.idiomatic: allowing cargo to pass through to Hankou;

sentences.zh: 曰行船直入。

translations.literal: namely, permitting ships to sail directly into Berdunier.
translations.idiomatic: and permitting vessels to navigate directly to Berdunier.

sentences.zh: 六年，廷議徇人請，將赦罪，力持不可，謂：「揆度機要在樞廷，折衝俎豆在總署，講信修睦在使臣。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, when the court considered acceding to the Russians' request and were about to pardon Chonghou's crime, [Xu] Tong firmly insisted it could not be done, saying: "Weighing strategy belongs in the Grand Council; parrying at the council table belongs in the Zongli Yamen; cultivating trust and harmony belongs to the envoys.
translations.idiomatic: In 1880, when the court debated yielding to Russian pressure and pardoning Chonghou, Xu Tong stood firm against it, arguing: "Strategic judgment rests with the Grand Council; negotiation at the council table rests with the Zongli Yamen; building trust and good relations rests with the envoys.

sentences.zh: 赦之而彼就範，猶裨國事；

translations.literal: If one pardons him and the other side then submits, it may still benefit state affairs;
translations.idiomatic: If a pardon brings them to terms, it may still serve the state;

sentences.zh: 若釁端仍不能弭，反失刑政大權。

translations.literal: but if trouble cannot still be quelled, one instead loses the great authority of penal administration.
translations.idiomatic: but if hostilities cannot be settled, we forfeit the crown's authority over punishment and law.

sentences.zh: 推原禍始，宜肅國憲。」

translations.literal: Tracing the origin of the calamity, the state constitution ought to be upheld."
translations.idiomatic: The root of the disaster should be traced to strict enforcement of national law."

sentences.zh: 又言：「今日用人之道，秉忠持正者為上，宅心樸實者次之。

translations.literal: He also said: "The way to employ men today: those who uphold loyalty and rectitude rank first; those whose hearts are plain and honest rank next.
translations.idiomatic: He added: "In appointing officials today, men who are loyal and upright should come first; men of plain and honest character should come next.

sentences.zh: 若以機權靈警，諳曉各國語言文字，遽目為通才，而責以鉅任，未有不僨且蹶者！」

translations.literal: If one suddenly regards men who are sharp in maneuver, clever and alert, and versed in the languages and scripts of the various nations as versatile talents and charges them with great responsibilities, there has never been a case where they did not collapse in failure!"
translations.idiomatic: To treat men merely because they are quick-witted and fluent in foreign tongues and scripts as universal talents fit for weighty office is to invite certain ruin."

sentences.zh: 不報。

translations.literal: There was no response.
translations.idiomatic: His advice went unheeded.

sentences.zh: 歷充翰林院掌院學士、上書房總師傅。

translations.literal: He successively served as Chancellor of the Hanlin Academy and Grand Tutor of the Upper Study Halls.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to be chancellor of the Hanlin Academy and grand tutor in the Upper Study Halls.

sentences.zh: 十五年，以吏部尚書協辦大學士，晉太子太保。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, as Minister of Personnel he served as Assistant Grand Secretary, and was promoted to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year (1889) he was appointed Minister of Personnel with concurrent duty as assistant grand secretary, then promoted to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，拜大學士。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year, he was appointed Grand Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year (1896) he was made a grand secretary.

sentences.zh: 有者，字，內務府。

translations.literal: There was Yu Shi, styled Xizhi, of the Han Chinese Banner in the Imperial Household Department.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Shi, whose style was Xizhi, served in the Imperial Household Department as a member of the Han Chinese Banner.

sentences.zh: 進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi degree holder.
translations.idiomatic: He held the jinshi degree.

sentences.zh: 官至都統，以講學為所傾服。

translations.literal: He rose to commandant-general at Urumqi; Xu Tong admired him for his scholarship.
translations.idiomatic: He eventually became commander-in-chief at Urumqi, and Xu Tong looked up to him as a scholar.

sentences.zh: 方太后議廢帝，立子為「大阿哥」，主之甚力，實皆本謀也。

translations.literal: When the Empress Dowager debated deposing the emperor and installing Prince Duan's son Pujun as "Great Heir Apparent," Xu Tong strongly advocated it; in truth all these plots originated with Yu Shi.
translations.idiomatic: During the debate over deposing the emperor and elevating Prince Duan's son Pujun as heir apparent, Xu Tong pushed hard for it—the scheme was Yu Shi's in essence.

sentences.zh: 既而被命照料，益親。

translations.literal: When Xu Tong was thereafter ordered to oversee [the heir], they became still closer to Prince Duan.
translations.idiomatic: Once Xu Tong was charged with supervising the boy, he grew even closer to Prince Duan.

sentences.zh: 各國不慊等所為，恚甚，圖報復。

translations.literal: The foreign powers were displeased with what Prince Duan and his circle had done; furious, he sought revenge.
translations.idiomatic: The powers resented Prince Duan's conduct and were determined on retaliation.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，起釁仇外，大喜，導之入都。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year, when the Boxers rose and turned hostility outward, [Prince Duan] was greatly pleased and guided them into the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In 1900, when the Boxers stirred up hatred of foreigners, Prince Duan was delighted and ushered them into Beijing.

sentences.zh: 謂：「當自此強矣！」

translations.literal: Xu Tong said: "China shall henceforth be strong!"
translations.idiomatic: Xu Tong declared: "From this day China will grow strong!"

sentences.zh: 至且親迓之。

translations.literal: He would even go out in person to welcome them.
translations.idiomatic: He even went out in person to welcome them.

sentences.zh: 然及其亂時，仍被劫掠、

translations.literal: Yet during the disorder he was still plundered.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when the chaos broke out, he was looted like everyone else.

sentences.zh: 之死，舉國稱冤，而則曰：「是死且有餘辜！」

translations.literal: At the deaths of Yuan Chang and Xu Jingcheng the whole country called it injustice, but Xu Tong said: "Even in death they still had guilt to spare!"
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Chang and Xu Jingcheng were executed, the nation called it a miscarriage of justice; Xu Tong said: "They deserved worse than death!"

sentences.zh: 時其子監刑，揚揚頗自得。

translations.literal: At the time his son Chengyu supervised the execution, looking quite pleased with himself.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chengyu oversaw the executions, swaggering with evident satisfaction.

sentences.zh: 剛毅，字子良，滿洲鑲藍旗人。

translations.literal: Gang Yi, styled Ziliang, was a man of the Bordered Blue Banner of the Manchus.
translations.idiomatic: Gang Yi, whose style was Ziliang, came from the Bordered Blue Banner of the Manchus.

sentences.zh: 以筆帖式累遷刑部郎中。

translations.literal: Starting as a clerk, he was promoted step by step to director in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from clerk through successive posts to director in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 諳悉例案，承審浙江餘杭縣民婦葛畢氏案，獲平反，按律定擬，得旨嘉獎。

translations.literal: Well versed in precedent cases, he took charge of trying the case of the commoner woman Ge Bishi of Yuhang County, Zhejiang, secured a reversal of judgment, fixed the sentence according to law, and received an imperial commendation.
translations.idiomatic: Fluent in legal precedent, he handled the case of Ge Bishi, a commoner woman of Yuhang in Zhejiang, secured her exoneration, and drafted a lawful sentence that earned imperial praise.

sentences.zh: 出為廣東惠潮嘉道，遷江西按察使，調直隸；

translations.literal: He went out as intendant of Huizhou, Chaozhou, and Jiazhou in Guangdong, was transferred to Jiangxi as surveillance commissioner, then to Zhili;
translations.idiomatic: He served as intendant of Huizhou, Chaozhou, and Jiazhou in Guangdong, then became surveillance commissioner in Jiangxi and was transferred to Zhili;

sentences.zh: 遷廣東布政使，調雲南。

translations.literal: was moved to Guangdong as provincial treasurer, then transferred to Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: then treasurer of Guangdong, and finally was posted to Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 光緒十一年，擢山西巡撫。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Guangxu he was promoted to governor of Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In 1885 he was appointed governor of Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 請設課吏館，手輯牧令須知諸書，分講習，詔飭行各省。

translations.literal: He requested establishment of an officials' training hall, personally compiled such works as What Magistrates Must Know, arranged lectures, and an edict ordered all provinces to follow suit.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed an academy for training officials, compiled manuals such as What Magistrates Must Know, organized instruction, and the court ordered every province to adopt the practice.

sentences.zh: 治套外屯田，建分段、開渠、設官三策。

translations.literal: For reclaiming garrison farms beyond the pass he proposed three measures: division into sections, opening canals, and appointing officials.
translations.idiomatic: For frontier garrison farming he advanced three policies: parceling land, digging canals, and appointing overseers.

sentences.zh: 明年，移撫江蘇。

translations.literal: The next year he was transferred to govern Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was made governor of Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 蘇患水祲，先後濬蘊藻河、吳淞江，以工代賑，民德之。

translations.literal: Jiangsu suffered flood and drought; he successively dredged the Yunzao River and the Wusong River, using labor relief in place of charity grain, and the people were grateful.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiangsu was stricken by flood and drought, he dredged the Yunzao and Wusong rivers and used public works as famine relief; the people were grateful.

sentences.zh: 調廣東。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: He was then transferred to Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 二十年，召授軍機大臣，補禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he was summoned and appointed Grand Councilor, with concurrent appointment as Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In 1894 he was recalled to the Grand Council and made Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，以工部尚書協辦大學士，疏陳實倉廩，嚴保甲，罷不急官。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year, as Minister of Works he served as Assistant Grand Secretary; in memorials he urged filling granaries, tightening the baojia system, and abolishing nonessential offices.
translations.idiomatic: In 1898, as Minister of Works and assistant grand secretary, he memorialized to fill granaries, tighten local security networks, and cut superfluous posts.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，按事江南及廣東諸省。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he conducted investigations in Jiangnan and the Guangdong provinces.
translations.idiomatic: In 1899 he toured Jiangnan and Guangdong on inspection.

sentences.zh: 迭疏請籌長江防務，籌餉練兵，清理財政，及整頓地方一切事宜，詔皆飭行。

translations.literal: He repeatedly memorialized to plan Yangtze defenses, raise funds and train troops, clear up finances, and put in order all local affairs; edicts ordered all to be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: He sent repeated memorials on Yangtze defenses, military funding and training, fiscal reform, and local administration; the throne ordered every item implemented.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，拳亂作，命趙舒翹及剛毅馳往近畿一帶查辦解散，及還京覆命，而宣戰詔已先下矣。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year the Boxer disturbance broke out; Zhao Shuqiao and Gang Yi were ordered to hurry to the near capital region to investigate and disband them; when they returned to the capital to report, the war declaration had already been issued.
translations.idiomatic: In 1900, when the Boxer uprising erupted, Zhao Shuqiao and Gang Yi were dispatched to the capital outskirts to investigate and disperse the movement; by the time they returned to report, the declaration of war had already been issued.

sentences.zh: 匪集都城，肆焚殺，時方稱義民，亡敢誰何。

translations.literal: The bandits gathered in the capital and wantonly burned and killed; at the time they were called righteous people, and no one dared challenge them.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels massed in the capital, burning and killing at will; hailed as patriotic militia, they went unchecked.

sentences.zh: 載漪等復疏言：「雪恥強國，在此一舉！」

translations.literal: Zaiyi and others again memorialized: "To wipe away disgrace and strengthen the state—this one stroke suffices!"
translations.idiomatic: Prince Duan and his allies memorialized again: "National humiliation can be wiped away and the state strengthened in this single stroke!"

sentences.zh: 又盛推拳民忠勇，有神術，可用。

translations.literal: They also lavishly praised the Boxers' loyalty and courage, claiming they had divine arts and could be used.
translations.idiomatic: They lavishly praised the Boxers as loyal, brave, possessed of magic, and fit for service.

sentences.zh: 太后愈信之，因命剛毅、載勳統之，比於官軍。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager believed them all the more and therefore ordered Gang Yi and Zaiyi to command them, ranking them with the regular army.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager believed them still more and put Gang Yi and Zaiyi in command, treating the Boxers as the equal of regular troops.

sentences.zh: 然匪專殺自如，勿能問，且擾禁城，日焚劫不止。

translations.literal: Yet the bandits killed as they pleased without restraint; none could call them to account, and they even disturbed the Forbidden City, with burning and looting daily unceasing.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the rebels killed as they pleased, beyond anyone's control, harrying even the Forbidden City with daily arson and looting.

sentences.zh: 詔各軍營會拏正法，盡拆所設神壇，並諭責剛毅、董福祥親自開導，勒令解散，卒不能阻。

translations.literal: An edict ordered all camps jointly to seize and execute according to law, tear down all altars they had set up, and also rebuked Gang Yi and Dong Fuxiang to guide them in person and compel disbandment—yet in the end they could not stop them.
translations.idiomatic: Edicts ordered every garrison to arrest and execute offenders, tear down their altars, and commanded Gang Yi and Dong Fuxiang personally to disband the movement—yet nothing could stop it.

sentences.zh: 各國聯軍入犯，兩宮西狩，剛毅扈行至太原。

translations.literal: When the allied armies of the various nations invaded, the two palaces went west on tour; Gang Yi escorted them as far as Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: When the allied armies invaded, the court fled west; Gang Yi escorted the empresses as far as Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 車駕欲之西安，又從。

translations.literal: When the imperial procession wished to go to Xi'an, he followed again.
translations.idiomatic: When the court decided to continue to Xi'an, he went along.

sentences.zh: 道遘疾，還至侯馬鎮，死。

translations.literal: On the road he fell ill, returned to Houma Town, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He fell ill on the road, turned back to Houma, and died there.

sentences.zh: 其後各國請懲禍首，以先死免議，追奪原官。

translations.literal: Afterward the various nations demanded punishment of the chief culprits; because he had died first he was spared discussion, but his former offices were posthumously stripped.
translations.idiomatic: Later the powers demanded the chief culprits be punished; his prior death spared formal proceedings, but his offices were posthumously revoked.

sentences.zh: 趙舒翹，字展如，陝西長安人。

translations.literal: Zhao Shuqiao, styled Zhanru, was a native of Chang'an in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Shuqiao, whose style was Zhanru, came from Chang'an in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 同治十三年進士，授刑部主事，遷員外郎。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the thirteenth year of Tongzhi, he was appointed a principal clerk in the Ministry of Justice and was promoted to vice director.
translations.idiomatic: He took his jinshi degree in 1874, entered the Ministry of Justice as a principal clerk, and rose to vice director.

sentences.zh: 讞河南王樹汶獄，承旨研辨，獲平反，巡撫李鶴年以下譴謫有差。

translations.literal: He reported on the Henan case of Wang Shuwen; following the imperial order he investigated and secured a reversal of judgment, and Governor Li Henian and those below him were censured and demoted to varying degrees.
translations.idiomatic: In the Henan case of Wang Shuwen he followed imperial orders, secured a reversal, and Governor Li Henian and his subordinates were punished in varying degrees.

sentences.zh: 居刑曹十年，多所纂定，其議服制及婦女離異諸條，能傅古義，為時所誦。

translations.literal: He spent ten years in the penal offices and compiled many regulations; his discussions of mourning garb and of women's divorce and separation could transmit ancient meaning and were recited in his time.
translations.idiomatic: After ten years in the penal bureaucracy he codified many rules; his treatises on mourning dress and on divorce and separation for women were praised for recovering classical principles.

sentences.zh: 光緒十二年，以郎中出知安徽鳳陽府。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Guangxu he went out from his directorship to serve as prefect of Fengyang in Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: In 1886 he left the ministry as a director to become prefect of Fengyang in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 皖北水祲，割俸助賑。

translations.literal: Northern Anhui suffered flood and drought; he cut his salary to aid relief.
translations.idiomatic: When northern Anhui was stricken by flood and drought, he donated his salary to relief efforts.

sentences.zh: 課最，擢浙江溫處道，再遷布政使。

translations.literal: Rated highest in evaluation, he was promoted to intendant of Wenzhou and Taichou in Zhejiang, then again transferred to provincial treasurer.
translations.idiomatic: Rated top in performance reviews, he was made intendant of Wenzhou and Taizhou in Zhejiang, then provincial treasurer.

sentences.zh: 二十年，擢江蘇巡撫。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he was promoted to governor of Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: In 1894 he was appointed governor of Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 捕治太湖匪酋葉子春，餘黨股栗；

translations.literal: He captured and punished the bandit chieftain Ye Zichun on Lake Tai; the remaining gangs trembled;
translations.idiomatic: He captured the Lake Tai bandit leader Ye Zichun, and the remaining gangs trembled;

sentences.zh: 復為籌善後策，弊風漸革。

translations.literal: he also devised policies for aftermath, and corrupt practices were gradually reformed.
translations.idiomatic: he devised follow-up policies, and local abuses were gradually curbed.

sentences.zh: 明年，改訂日本條約，牒請總署重民生，所言皆切中。

translations.literal: The next year, when the treaty with Japan was revised, he memorialized the Zongli Yamen to stress livelihood of the people; everything he said hit the mark.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, during revision of the Japanese treaty, he urged the Zongli Yamen to put the people's livelihood first—every point he made was on target.

sentences.zh: 是時朝廷矜慎庶獄，以舒翹諳律令，召為刑部左侍郎。

translations.literal: At that time the court was cautious about common criminal cases; because Shuqiao was versed in statutes, he was summoned as Left Vice Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: The court was then cautious about ordinary criminal cases and recalled him as Left Vice Minister of Justice for his mastery of law.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，晉尚書，督辦礦務、鐵路。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he was promoted to minister and supervised mining and railways.
translations.idiomatic: In 1898 he was promoted to minister and placed in charge of mining and railways.

sentences.zh: 明年，命入總理各國事務衙門，充軍機大臣。

translations.literal: The next year he was ordered into the Zongli Yamen and appointed Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he entered the Zongli Yamen and joined the Grand Council.

sentences.zh: 拳匪據涿州，舒翹被命馳往解散；

translations.literal: When the Boxers seized Zhuozhou, Shuqiao was ordered to hurry there to disband them;
translations.idiomatic: When the Boxers occupied Zhuozhou, Shuqiao was sent to disperse them;

sentences.zh: 匪眾堅請褫提督聶士成職，剛毅踵至，許之。

translations.literal: the bandits firmly demanded dismissal of Grand Commissioner Nie Shicheng; Gang Yi followed and granted it.
translations.idiomatic: the rebels demanded Grand Commissioner Nie Shicheng be removed; Gang Yi arrived after him and agreed.

sentences.zh: 匪既入京，攻使館。

translations.literal: Once the bandits entered the capital they attacked the legations.
translations.idiomatic: Once the rebels entered Beijing they besieged the legations.

sentences.zh: 聯軍至，李秉衡兵敗，太后乃令王文韶與舒翹詣使館通殷勤，為議款計。

translations.literal: When the allied armies arrived and Li Bingheng's troops were defeated, the Empress Dowager then ordered Wang Wenshao and Shuqiao to go to the legations with courteous messages as a plan to negotiate terms.
translations.idiomatic: When the allied armies arrived and Li Bingheng's force was routed, the Empress Dowager ordered Wang Wenshao and Shuqiao to visit the legations with courtesies to open peace talks.

sentences.zh: 文韶以老辭，舒翹曰：「臣望淺，不如文韶！」

translations.literal: Wenshao declined on account of age; Shuqiao said: "Your servant's standing is slight—I am not the equal of Wenshao!"
translations.idiomatic: Wenshao pleaded old age; Shuqiao said: "My standing is too slight—I am no match for Wenshao!"

sentences.zh: 卒不往。

translations.literal: In the end he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he never went.

sentences.zh: 旋隨扈至西安。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he followed the imperial procession to Xi'an.
translations.idiomatic: He soon followed the court's flight to Xi'an.

sentences.zh: 聯軍索辦罪魁，乃褫職留任，尋改斬監候。

translations.literal: When the allied armies demanded punishment of the chief culprits, he was stripped of office but kept on duty, then changed to imprisonment awaiting decapitation.
translations.idiomatic: When the allies demanded the chief culprits be punished, he was stripped of rank but kept under detention, then sentenced to imprisonment awaiting execution.

sentences.zh: 次年，各國索益亟，西安士民集數百人為舒翹請命，上聞，賜自盡，命岑春煊監視。

translations.literal: The next year the various nations pressed their demands more urgently; several hundred gentry and commoners of Xi'an gathered to plead for Shuqiao's life; when this reached the throne he was granted suicide, with Cen Chunxuan ordered to supervise.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the powers pressed harder; hundreds of Xi'an residents petitioned for his life, but the throne ordered him to take his own life under Cen Chunxuan's supervision.

sentences.zh: 舒翹故不袒匪，又痛老母九十餘見此慘禍，頗自悔恨。

translations.literal: Shuqiao had never openly sided with the bandits, yet he also grieved that his mother, over ninety, should witness this calamity, and he deeply repented.
translations.idiomatic: Shuqiao had never openly sided with the Boxers, yet he was tormented that his mother, past ninety, should see this tragedy, and he bitterly repented.

sentences.zh: 初飲金，更飲以鴆，久之乃絕，其妻仰藥以殉。

translations.literal: At first he drank gold; then he was given poison; only after a long while did he expire, and his wife took medicine and died with him.
translations.idiomatic: He first swallowed gold, then was given poison; death came only after a long struggle, and his wife took poison to join him.

sentences.zh: 啟秀，字穎之，庫雅拉氏，滿洲正白旗人。

translations.literal: Qi Xiu, styled Yingzhi, of the Kuyala clan, was a man of the Plain White Banner of the Manchus.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Xiu, whose style was Yingzhi, came from the Kuyala clan of the Plain White Banner.

sentences.zh: 以孝聞。

translations.literal: He was known for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: He was famed for filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 同治四年進士，選庶吉士，散館改刑部主事，累遷內閣學士。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the fourth year of Tongzhi, he was selected as a bachelor of the Hanlin, and after leaving the academy was made a principal clerk in the Ministry of Justice, rising step by step to a bachelor of the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He took his jinshi in 1865, entered the Hanlin Academy, then the Ministry of Justice, and rose to grand secretariat bachelor.

sentences.zh: 光緒五年，授工部右侍郎，調盛京刑部。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Guangxu he was appointed Right Vice Minister of Works and transferred to the Penal Department of Mukden.
translations.idiomatic: In 1879 he became Right Vice Minister of Works and was transferred to the Mukden penal administration.

sentences.zh: 吉林將軍銘​​安被彈劾，啟秀白其誣，轉戶部。

translations.literal: When General Ming'an of Jilin was impeached, Qi Xiu declared his innocence and was transferred to the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: When General Ming'an of Jilin was impeached, Qi Xiu cleared him of false charges and was moved to the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 論者以按銘安事多徇芘，攻甚力，命崇綺覆按，無左驗，免議。

translations.literal: Critics held that in handling Ming'an's case he had often shown favoritism and attacked him fiercely; Chongqi was ordered to reinvestigate, found no corroborating evidence, and he was spared censure.
translations.idiomatic: Critics accused him of favoritism in the Ming'an case; Chongqi reinvestigated, found no proof, and Qi Xiu escaped punishment.

sentences.zh: 東省練新軍，倚餉京師，閻敬銘掌戶部，方規節帑，未應也。

translations.literal: The eastern provinces were training new armies and relied on funds from the capital; Yan Jingming controlled the Ministry of Revenue and was planning to economize the treasury, and had not yet responded.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern provinces were raising new armies and depended on Beijing for pay; Yan Jingming at the Ministry of Revenue was cutting expenses and had not yet approved the funds.

sentences.zh: 啟秀力言，始獲請，歲發四十萬濟之。

translations.literal: Qi Xiu spoke forcefully and only then obtained approval; four hundred thousand taels were sent yearly to support them.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Xiu pressed the case until approval came: four hundred thousand taels a year were allocated.

sentences.zh: 二十年，拜理籓院尚書。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he was appointed Minister of the Court of Colonial Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In 1894 he was made Minister of the Court of Colonial Affairs.

sentences.zh: 中、日和議成，將換約，啟秀疏請：「條約宜緩發，先商諸各國，杜後患。」

translations.literal: When the Sino-Japanese peace was concluded and the treaty was to be exchanged, Qi Xiu memorialized: "The treaty ought to be issued slowly; first consult the various nations to forestall later troubles."
translations.idiomatic: When the Sino-Japanese peace was concluded and ratification neared, Qi Xiu urged: "Ratification should be delayed until other powers are consulted, to forestall future trouble."

sentences.zh: 不報。

translations.literal: There was no response.
translations.idiomatic: His advice went unheeded.

sentences.zh: 敖漢王達木林達爾達克鑑朝陽覆轍，自請增練蒙軍。

translations.literal: The Prince of Aohan, Damulin Da'erdake, seeing Chaoyang's repeated disasters, requested on his own to increase training of Mongol troops.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Aohan, Damulin Da'erdake, seeing Chaoyang's troubles repeat, volunteered to expand Mongol troop training.

sentences.zh: 言者論其苛派蒙眾，謀不軌，啟秀為訟其冤。

translations.literal: Memorialists argued that he harshly levied on the Mongol populace and plotted sedition; Qi Xiu pleaded his innocence.
translations.idiomatic: Critics charged him with extorting the Mongols and plotting rebellion; Qi Xiu defended him.

sentences.zh: 敖漢王雖奪扎薩克秩，而其子獲嗣，以故大得蒙眾心。

translations.literal: Although the Prince of Aohan was stripped of his jasak rank, his son succeeded to it; for this reason he greatly won the hearts of the Mongol masses.
translations.idiomatic: Though the prince lost his jasak title, his son inherited it, and he retained strong support among the Mongols.

sentences.zh: 充總管內務府大臣。

translations.literal: He served as superintendent grand minister of the Imperial Household Department.
translations.idiomatic: He became superintendent of the Imperial Household Department.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，授禮部尚書，疏陳釐正文體，倡明聖學。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he was appointed Minister of Rites; in memorials he urged correcting literary forms and promoting sagely learning.
translations.idiomatic: In 1898 he was made Minister of Rites and memorialized to reform literary style and promote classical learning.

sentences.zh: 命充軍機大臣兼總理各國事務衙門。

translations.literal: He was ordered to serve as Grand Councilor with concurrent duty in the Zongli Yamen.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed to the Grand Council and the Zongli Yamen.

sentences.zh: 啟秀端謹有風操，為徐桐所賞。

translations.literal: Qi Xiu was upright, careful, and possessed moral integrity; Xu Tong admired him.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Xiu was upright and principled, and Xu Tong held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 自政變後，桐最被盻遇，欲引參機務，乃舉啟秀自代。

translations.literal: After the political coup Xu Tong was most favored; wishing to draw him into state affairs, he recommended Qi Xiu to replace himself.
translations.idiomatic: After the 1898 coup Xu Tong was the Empress Dowager's favorite; wanting a proxy in policy, he recommended Qi Xiu to take his place.

sentences.zh: 已而拳亂作，董福祥攻使館不下，啟秀薦五台僧禦敵，頗附和之。

translations.literal: Soon the Boxer disturbance broke out; Dong Fuxiang could not take the legations; Qi Xiu recommended a monk of Wutai to repel the enemy and largely went along with the plan.
translations.idiomatic: When the Boxer rising erupted and Dong Fuxiang failed to overrun the legations, Qi Xiu recommended a Wutai monk to fight the foreigners and lent his support.

sentences.zh: 逮兩宮狩西安，啟秀以母病弗克從。

translations.literal: When the two palaces went on tour to Xi'an, Qi Xiu could not follow because his mother was ill.
translations.idiomatic: When the court fled to Xi'an, Qi Xiu stayed behind because his mother was ill.

sentences.zh: 日本軍拘啟秀及徐承煜嚴守之，承煜，桐子也。

translations.literal: The Japanese army detained Qi Xiu and Xu Chengyu and kept them under strict guard; Chengyu was Xu Tong's son.
translations.idiomatic: Japanese troops seized Qi Xiu and Xu Chengyu and held them under close guard; Chengyu was Xu Tong's son.

sentences.zh: 朝旨褫職，而各國猶言罪魁不可縱。

translations.literal: An imperial order stripped them of office, yet the various nations still said the chief culprits could not be spared.
translations.idiomatic: The court stripped them of rank, but the powers insisted the chief culprits must not go unpunished.

sentences.zh: 明年，正法命下，日軍官置酒為餞，席次，傳詔旨，啟秀神色自若，曰：​​「即此已邀聖恩矣！」

translations.literal: The next year the order for lawful execution was issued; a Japanese officer set out wine as a farewell; at the banquet, when the edict was announced, Qi Xiu's expression was calm as he said: "Even this already invites imperial grace!"
translations.idiomatic: The following year the execution order came down. A Japanese officer gave him a farewell feast; when the edict was read, Qi Xiu remained composed and said: "Even this is already imperial favor!"

sentences.zh: 肅衣冠赴菜市。

translations.literal: He put on formal dress and hat and went to the Vegetable Market.
translations.idiomatic: He dressed in full court robes and walked to the execution ground at Caishikou.

sentences.zh: 啟秀宅近日本權領地，日官與語，當善芘其家，第曰：「厚意可感。」

translations.literal: Qi Xiu's residence was near the Japanese concession; a Japanese official spoke with him, saying his family would be well protected; he only said: "Your generous intent is deeply felt."
translations.idiomatic: His home lay near the Japanese concession; a Japanese official promised to protect his family. Qi Xiu replied only: "Your kindness moves me."

sentences.zh: 他無復言，遂就戮。

translations.literal: He said nothing more and then submitted to execution.
translations.idiomatic: He said nothing more and went to his death.

sentences.zh: 英年，字菊儕，姓何氏，隸內務府，為漢軍正白旗人。

translations.literal: Ying Nian, styled Juyi, bore the surname He, was attached to the Imperial Household Department, and was a man of the Han Chinese Plain White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Ying Nian, whose style was Juyi, came from the He clan of the Han Chinese Plain White Banner and served in the Imperial Household Department.

sentences.zh: 以貢生考取筆帖式，累遷郎中兼護軍參領。

translations.literal: As a tribute student he passed the examination for clerk and was promoted step by step to director with concurrent duty as adjutant of the guard.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service as a tribute student, passed the clerk examination, and rose to director with a concurrent post as guard adjutant.

sentences.zh: 光緒中，歷奉宸苑卿、左翼總兵、正紅旗漢軍副都統、工部右侍郎，調戶部。

translations.literal: During Guangxu he successively served as Director of the Imperial Parks, Left Wing Commander-in-Chief, Vice Commander-in-Chief of the Han Chinese Bordered Red Banner, and Right Vice Minister of Works, then was transferred to the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Under Guangxu he held posts including Director of the Imperial Parks, Left Wing commander-in-chief, vice commander of the Han Chinese Bordered Red Banner, and Right Vice Minister of Works before moving to the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 拳匪亂作，以英年、載瀾副載勳、剛毅統之。

translations.literal: When the Boxer disturbance broke out, Ying Nian and Zai Lan were made deputies to Zaiyi and Gang Yi to command them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Boxer rising erupted, Ying Nian and Zai Lan were appointed deputies to Zaiyi and Gang Yi in commanding the movement.

sentences.zh: 載勳等出示，招致義民助攻使館，英年弗能阻，匪益橫，任意戕殺官民。

translations.literal: Zaiyi and others went out and summoned righteous people to assist in attacking the legations; Ying Nian could not stop them, and the bandits grew still more arrogant, killing officials and commoners at will.
translations.idiomatic: Zaiyi and his allies paraded through the streets recruiting militia to attack the legations; Ying Nian could not stop them, and the rebels grew bolder, slaughtering officials and civilians at will.

sentences.zh: 聯軍既陷京師，兩宮幸西安，英年充行在查營大臣，旋授左都御史。

translations.literal: After the allied armies took the capital, the two palaces went to Xi'an; Ying Nian served as traveling inspector of camps and was soon appointed Left Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: After Beijing fell, the court fled to Xi'an; Ying Nian served as traveling inspector of camps and was soon made Left Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 行次猗氏，知縣玉寶供張不備，疏劾之。

translations.literal: Passing through Yishi, he found the magistrate Yubao's provisions for the imperial procession inadequate and memorialized to impeach him.
translations.idiomatic: At Yishi he found Magistrate Yubao's arrangements for the imperial procession inadequate and impeached him.

sentences.zh: 款成，各使議懲首禍，英年褫職論斬，羈西安獄，尋賜自盡。

translations.literal: When terms were settled the various ministers discussed punishing the chief instigators; Ying Nian was stripped of office and sentenced to decapitation, detained in Xi'an prison, and soon granted suicide.
translations.idiomatic: After peace was made the foreign ministers demanded punishment of the ringleaders; Ying Nian was stripped of rank, sentenced to death, imprisoned in Xi'an, and soon ordered to take his own life.

sentences.zh: 時官吏多信，布政使獨力主剿辦，嚴定州縣查緝匪懲戒辦法。

translations.literal: At that time most officials in Zhili believed in the Boxers; only the provincial treasurer Ting Jie alone insisted on suppression and strictly fixed methods for counties and prefectures to search out and punish the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Most Zhili officials then believed in the Boxers; only Provincial Treasurer Ting Jie insisted on suppression and laid down strict county-level measures to hunt and punish them.

sentences.zh: 遽奉詔開缺回，匪愈橫。

translations.literal: He was suddenly ordered by edict to vacate his post and return to the capital; the bandits grew still more arrogant.
translations.idiomatic: An edict suddenly recalled him to Beijing, and the Boxers grew bolder still.

sentences.zh: 居，稱「舉國第一壇」，為匪魁，二人者炫神術，為妄妖言相煽誘，不之問。

translations.literal: Zhang Decheng dwelt at Duliang, styled "the foremost altar in the realm," and was chieftain of the bandits; the two men boasted of divine arts and incited one another with wild demonic talk, yet Yu Lu did not question them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Decheng at Duliang styled himself head of "the foremost altar in the realm," and he and Cao Futian traded boasts of magic and sedition; Yu Lu looked the other way.

sentences.zh: 已，复致書請餉二十萬，自任滅外人，馳檄召之，於是二人出入節署，與抗禮。

translations.literal: Before long they again wrote requesting two hundred thousand taels in funds, undertaking themselves to destroy the foreigners; Yu Lu sent urgent dispatches summoning them, and thereafter the two men came and went at the governor's yamen, treating him as an equal in ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: They soon demanded two hundred thousand taels, promising to destroy the foreigners; Yu Lu summoned them by urgent dispatch, and thereafter they came and went at his yamen as his equals.

sentences.zh: 當是時，城匪至可三萬人，呼嘯周衢市，又以熒眾，每入夜，家家懸紅燈，謂「迎仙姑」。

translations.literal: At that time the bandits in the city may have reached thirty thousand; they roared through the streets and markets; moreover the Red Lantern Society inflamed the masses, and each night every household hung red lamps, saying they were "welcoming the Immortal Maiden."
translations.idiomatic: Boxers in the city may have numbered thirty thousand, roaring through the streets; the Red Lantern Society stirred the crowds, and every night households hung red lamps to "welcome the Immortal Maiden."

sentences.zh: 頃之，各國兵艦大集，匪猶群聚督轅求槍砲，命詣軍械所任自擇，盡攫以去。

translations.literal: Before long the warships of the various nations gathered in force; the bandits still thronged the governor's yamen demanding guns and cannon; Yu Lu ordered them to the arsenal to choose as they pleased, and they seized everything and left.
translations.idiomatic: Soon foreign warships massed offshore, yet the Boxers still crowded the governor's yamen demanding arms; Yu Lu sent them to the arsenal to take what they wanted, and they carried everything away.

sentences.zh: 而聯軍絡繹登岸，索砲台，懼，疏告急，請敕來援。

translations.literal: Meanwhile the allied armies landed in an unbroken stream and demanded the forts; Yu Lu was afraid, memorialized in urgent alarm, and requested an edict summoning Dong Fuxiang to aid.
translations.idiomatic: Allied troops landed in force and demanded the Taku forts; terrified, Yu Lu sent urgent memorials begging the throne to summon Dong Fuxiang.

sentences.zh: 聯軍索益堅，提督不允，戰失利，而且上團民殺敵狀，於是朝廷以團民為可恃，宣戰詔書遂下，而不知已先數日失矣。

translations.literal: The allied demands grew still firmer; Grand Commissioner Luo Rongguang refused; the battle was lost; yet Yu Lu also reported the Tianjin militia's kills of the enemy, and so the court believed the militia could be relied upon—the declaration of war was issued, not knowing the forts had already fallen several days before.
translations.idiomatic: The allies pressed harder; Commissioner Luo Rongguang refused and was defeated; yet Yu Lu also reported Tianjin militia victories, and the court, believing the militia dependable, declared war—unaware the Taku forts had fallen days earlier.

sentences.zh: 又報大捷，盛張匪功，發帑金十萬犒團，更薦、於朝，飾戰狀，獲賞頭品秩、花翎、黃馬褂。

translations.literal: He again reported a great victory, lavishly extolled the bandits' merit, issued one hundred thousand taels from the treasury to reward the militia, and further recommended Decheng and Futian at court, embellishing battle reports; they received rewards of top rank, peacock feather, and yellow riding jacket.
translations.idiomatic: He reported another great victory, lavished praise on the Boxers, distributed one hundred thousand taels to reward the militia, and recommended Decheng and Futian to the court with embellished battle accounts; they were given top rank, peacock feathers, and yellow riding jackets.

sentences.zh: 事急，官軍戰車站，敗績，退保。

translations.literal: As matters grew urgent the regular army fought at the railway station, suffered defeat, and fell back to defend Beicang.
translations.idiomatic: As the crisis deepened the regular army fought at the railway station, was routed, and fell back to Beicang.

sentences.zh: 閱三日，城陷，、挾貲走，卒係而罪之。

translations.literal: Within three days the city fell; Decheng and Futian fled with their loot, but in the end were seized and punished.
translations.idiomatic: Three days later the city fell; Decheng and Futian fled with their plunder but were eventually captured and punished.

sentences.zh: 飛章自劾，詔革職留任。

translations.literal: Yu Lu sent a flying memorial impeaching himself; an edict stripped him of office but kept him on duty.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Lu urgently memorialized to impeach himself; the throne stripped his rank but left him in post.

sentences.zh: 踰月，失，又退，遂自殺。

translations.literal: After a month Beicang was lost; he retreated again to Yangcun, and then committed suicide.
translations.idiomatic: A month later Beicang fell; he retreated to Yangcun and took his own life.

sentences.zh: 和議成，奪職。

translations.literal: When peace was concluded his offices were posthumously stripped.
translations.idiomatic: After peace was made his offices were formally revoked.

sentences.zh: 是時撫，適有仇西教，獎借之，戕二教士。

translations.literal: At that time Li Bingheng was governor of Shandong; there happened to be hostility toward Western religion, and he encouraged and indulged it, killing two German missionaries.
translations.idiomatic: Li Bingheng was then governor of Shandong; anti-Christian sentiment ran high, and he encouraged it, resulting in the killing of two German missionaries.

sentences.zh: 廷議以官久，諳河務，擢代之。

translations.literal: The court considered that Yu Xian had long served in Shandong and understood river works, and promoted him to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: The court judged Yu Xian's long service in Shandong and knowledge of river works qualified him, and appointed him in Li's place.

sentences.zh: 既蒞事，護尤力。

translations.literal: Once he took up affairs he protected the Big Sword Society with especial force.
translations.idiomatic: Once in office he shielded the Big Sword Society more zealously than ever.

sentences.zh: 匪首搆亂，倡言滅教。

translations.literal: The bandit chieftain Zhu Hongdeng stirred disorder and preached destroying Christianity.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel leader Zhu Hongdeng stirred up trouble and preached the extermination of Christianity.

sentences.zh: 令知府按問，匪擊殺官軍數十人，自稱。

translations.literal: Yu Xian ordered the prefect to investigate; the bandits killed several dozen government troops and styled themselves the Boxer militia.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Xian ordered the prefect to investigate; the rebels killed dozens of government troops and proclaimed themselves the Boxer militia.

sentences.zh: 毓賢為更名曰「團」，團建旗幟，皆署「毓」字。

translations.literal: Yu Xian renamed them "militia"; the militia raised banners, all marked with the character "Yu."
translations.idiomatic: Yu Xian rechristened them "militia"; their banners all bore the character for his surname.

sentences.zh: 教士乞保護，置勿問。

translations.literal: Missionaries begged for protection; he set the matter aside and did not inquire.
translations.idiomatic: Missionaries pleaded for protection; he ignored them.

sentences.zh: 匪浸熾，使詰總署，乃徵還。

translations.literal: As the bandits grew daily more powerful, the French minister pressed the Zongli Yamen, and Yu Xian was recalled.
translations.idiomatic: As the movement spread, the French minister protested to the Zongli Yamen, and Yu Xian was recalled to Beijing.

sentences.zh: 至則謁、、大學士，盛言民忠勇得神助。

translations.literal: On arrival he paid calls on Prince Duan, Prince Zhuang, and Grand Secretary Gang Yi, lavishly praising the people's loyalty, courage, and divine aid.
translations.idiomatic: In Beijing he visited Prince Duan, Prince Zhuang, and Grand Secretary Gang Yi, praising the militia's loyalty, courage, and supernatural aid.

sentences.zh: 俄拜巡撫之命，於是術漸被。

translations.literal: Soon he received appointment as governor of Shanxi, and thereafter Boxer arts gradually spread there.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed governor of Shanxi, and Boxer practices spread across the province.

sentences.zh: 府縣上書言匪事，痛斥之，匪益熾。

translations.literal: Prefectures and counties memorialized on the bandit situation; he rebuked them sharply, and the bandits grew still more powerful.
translations.idiomatic: Local officials reported on the Boxers; he rebuked them harshly, and the movement grew stronger.

sentences.zh: 更命製鋼刀數百，賜拳童令演習，其酋出入撫署，款若上賓。

translations.literal: He further ordered several hundred steel knives made and bestowed on boxing youths for drill; their chieftains came and went at the governor's yamen, entertained like honored guests.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered hundreds of steel blades forged for young boxers to practice with; rebel leaders came and went at his yamen, entertained like honored guests.

sentences.zh: 居無何，朝旨申命保教民，陽遵旨，行下各縣文書稠疊，教士咸感悅。

translations.literal: Before long an imperial order again commanded protection of Christian people; Yu Xian outwardly obeyed, sent down documents to every county in thick stacks, and the missionaries were all gratified.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the court again ordered protection of Christians; Yu Xian ostensibly complied, flooding the counties with reassuring documents, and the missionaries were reassured.

sentences.zh: 未幾，又命傳致教士駐省城，曰：「縣中兵力薄，防疏失也。」

translations.literal: Before long he again ordered missionaries summoned to stay in the provincial capital, saying: "In the counties military strength is slight and defense is lax."
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered missionaries brought to the provincial capital, saying: "County garrisons are too weak to protect you."

sentences.zh: 教士先後至者七十餘人，乃扃聚一室，衛以兵，時致蔬果。

translations.literal: More than seventy missionaries arrived one after another; he then shut them together in one room, guarded them with troops, and from time to time sent fruits and vegetables.
translations.idiomatic: More than seventy missionaries arrived; he locked them in a single room under armed guard and sent them fruit and vegetables from time to time.

sentences.zh: 一日，忽冠服拜母，泣不可止，曰：「男勤國事，不復能顧身家矣！」

translations.literal: One day he suddenly put on cap and robes and bowed to his mother, weeping without cease, saying: "Your son is laboring for state affairs and can no longer look after family and person!"
translations.idiomatic: One day he appeared in full court dress before his mother, weeping uncontrollably: "I am consumed by affairs of state and can no longer protect our family!"

sentences.zh: 問之不語。

translations.literal: When asked he would not speak.
translations.idiomatic: Asked what he meant, he would not answer.

sentences.zh: 遽出，坐堂皇，呼七十餘人者至，令自承悔教，教民不肯承，乃悉率出斬之，婦孺就死，呼號聲不忍聞。

translations.literal: He rushed out, sat in the main hall, summoned the more than seventy persons, ordered them to confess repentance of Christianity; the Christians would not confess, and he then led them all out to be beheaded; women and children met death, and the cries were unbearable to hear.
translations.idiomatic: He rushed to the main hall, summoned the captives, and ordered them to renounce Christianity; when they refused, he had all of them beheaded—women and children among them—and their cries were unbearable.

sentences.zh: 聯軍既陷，請勤王，未及行，朝旨趣之再。

translations.literal: After the allied armies took Tianjin he requested to come to the throne's aid; before he could set out, imperial orders urged him twice.
translations.idiomatic: After Tianjin fell he asked to march to the emperor's aid; before he could depart, urgent orders from the court summoned him twice.

sentences.zh: 兩宮已西幸，遇諸塗，遂隨扈行。

translations.literal: The two palaces had already gone west; he met them on the road and then followed the imperial procession.
translations.idiomatic: The court had already fled west; he met the procession on the road and joined the flight.

sentences.zh: 和議成，聯軍指索罪魁，中外大臣復交章論劾，始褫職，戍。

translations.literal: When peace was concluded the allied armies pointed out and demanded the chief culprits; Chinese and foreign ministers again submitted joint memorials of impeachment; only then was he stripped of office and banished to Xinjiang.
translations.idiomatic: After peace was made the allies demanded the ringleaders; Chinese and foreign ministers memorialized again; only then was he stripped of rank and exiled to Xinjiang.

sentences.zh: 十二月，行抵，而正法命下。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, as he reached Gansu on the journey, the order for lawful execution was issued.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, as he reached Gansu, the execution order came down.

sentences.zh: 時權督。

translations.literal: At that time Li Tingxiao was acting governor of Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: Li Tingxiao was then acting governor of Gansu.

sentences.zh: 論曰：戊戌政變後，廢立議起，患外人為梗，遂欲仇之，而庚子匪之亂乘機作矣。

translations.literal: The commentator says: After the coup of 1898, debate over deposing the emperor and installing an heir arose; fearing foreigners as an obstruction, they wished to make them enemies, and the Boxer disturbance of 1900 seized the opportunity to break out.
translations.idiomatic: The historian comments: After the coup of 1898, the struggle over deposing the emperor revived; seeing foreigners as the obstacle, the court turned toward hostility, and the Boxer rising of 1900 erupted in that moment.

sentences.zh: 太后信其術，思倚以鋤敵而立威。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager believed their arts and thought to rely on them to cut down enemies and establish authority.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager believed in their magic and hoped to lean on them to destroy enemies and assert her power.

sentences.zh: 王公貴人各為其私，群奉意旨不敢違，大亂遂成。

translations.literal: Princes, dukes, and nobles each pursued private ends; all followed her intent and dared not disobey, and great disorder was thus accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: Princes and grandees each pursued private ends; all followed her will without dissent, and catastrophe followed.

sentences.zh: 及事敗，各國議懲首禍，等皆不能免。

translations.literal: When matters failed, the various nations discussed punishing the chief instigators, and Xu Tong and the others could none of them escape.
translations.idiomatic: When the cause collapsed, the powers demanded the ringleaders be punished, and Xu Tong and his circle could not escape.

sentences.zh: 逢君之惡，孽由自作。

translations.literal: They indulged the ruler's wickedness; the calamity was of their own making.
translations.idiomatic: They had indulged the ruler's worst impulses; the ruin was of their own making.

sentences.zh: 然刑賞聽命於人，何以立國哉？

translations.literal: Yet when punishment and reward obey others' commands, how can a state be established?
translations.idiomatic: Yet when punishments and rewards are dictated by foreign powers, what foundation remains for the state?
